To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) under conditions of linear STRS, the distribution of the energy of a pulse of the forward STRS is close to Gaussian, with a coefficient of variation that decreases as the pump pulse energy increases.

the statistical characteristics of the energies in forward and backward STRS differ in a number of ways, including the fact that the coefficient of variation of the backward STRSc pulses is higher than that of forward STRSc pulses.

(1) the statistical characteristics of the forward and backward first Stokes radiation pulses differ significantly, (2) the statistical properties of the forward first Stokes radiation pulse are consistent with quantum theory, and (3) stimulated Raman scattering causes fluctuations in the energy of the forward and the backward pump pulses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical properties of STRS pulses.
the statistical characteristics of the energies and intensities of the pulses of forward and back-ward STRS under linear, intermediate and nonlinear scattering conditions.
a study of the statistical properties of STRS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the statistical characteristics of the energy of STRS pulses depend on the degree of saturation of the scattering medium.

the statistical properties of the STRS pulse energies are determined by the statistical properties of fluctuations of the number of molecules participating in the STRS process, which in turn are determined by the properties of fluctuations of pump pulse energy.
the statistical properties of the energies of the forward STRS and pump pulses are determined by the quantum nature of STRS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that STRS is a stochastic process.

the statistical properties of the pulses of the forward STRS, backward STRS, and pump radiation were determined under linear, intermediate and nonlinear scattering conditions, and the dependences of these properties on the parameters of the scattering medium and of the pump radiation were established.
the energy of the STRS pulses is determined not only by the intensity of the pump pulses and by the properties of the scattering medium, but also by the statistical properties of the pump radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STRS gives rise to fluctuations of transmitted pump radiation, and these fluctuations can be characterized by the coefficient of variation and by the asymmetry of their distribution.
the statistical properties of the STRS pulses are different from those of the pump pulses, which is important for the development of the STRS theory and for the design of lasers based on STRS.
the energy of the forward STRS pulse is a function of the energy of its parent pulse and the energy of the energy of a forward STRS pulse can be determined from a knowledge of the pump pulse energy.
